_comment: Adversarial-review panel composition, as data. The driver (run-review.ps1) reads this to know which reviewers to run, with which wrapper, model, and reasoning effort. Swap or add reviewers HERE, not in code. INVARIANT: the active (enabled) reviewer set must span at least `minVendors` distinct vendors -- uncorrelated error across vendors is the entire point of the panel. v2: all vendors are subscription-backed CLIs (see `wrapper`); the metered-API wrappers are retained as `fallbackWrapper` for when a subscription is unavailable. See docs/METHODOLOGY-v2.md.

wrappers._comment: Each wrapper is a sibling .ps1. Required minimum parameters: -Instruction -DiffPath -FindingsPath -ContextPath -Model. Optional capabilities: -InstructionPath -Effort -RepoPath -OutPath -UsageSidecarPath. All return review text on stdout and non-zero on failure; the driver introspects optional parameters. Subscription-backed CLI wrappers are primary, with declared fallbacks only.

reviewers._comment: Anthropic reviewer #1 (Sonnet). Subscription-backed via Claude Code (Agent tool in-process) or `claude -p` (claude-review.ps1) on other hosts. Repo-aware and hard read-only (--permission-mode plan). Reviewer != judge: the Phase-3 judge is Opus, so a Sonnet reviewer keeps the anthropic axis decorrelated from the adjudicator.
reviewers.label: Claude Sonnet

reviewers._comment: Anthropic reviewer #2 (Fable 5). Same vendor as B -- a correlated, not independent, second vote, handled by vendor-weighted consensus (Phase-3 brief) and a merged Observatory row. Fable is now available in perpetuity on the Claude subscription. Canonical telemetry id: claude-fable-5.
reviewers.label: Claude Fable 5

reviewers._comment: OpenAI reviewer. PRIMARY = Codex CLI (codex-review.ps1), subscription-backed via a ChatGPT Pro login -- no metered credits. FALLBACK = openai-review.ps1 (direct Chat Completions API) for when no subscription is available; the driver falls back on primary non-zero exit and flags the run degraded-to-API. Repo-aware and HARD read-only (codex exec --sandbox read-only). Note: codex model ids differ from the API model id below; the codex wrapper uses the subscription's default model unless the id is codex-native, and records `model` for telemetry grouping only.
reviewers.label: GPT (Codex)

reviewers._comment: Moonshot reviewer. Subscription-backed via the Kimi Code CLI (kimi-review.ps1), Allegretto OAuth login -- no API fallback. The wrapper explicitly pins kimi-code/kimi-for-coding (K2.7 Coding, Standard), independent of the user's current CLI default. The highspeed selector spends roughly 3x credits; kimi-code/k3 is a distinct 1M-context model. repoAccess is false because Kimi has no per-invocation read-only flag; the wrapper runs hermetically with copied context.
reviewers.label: Kimi (standard)

reviewers._comment: Google reviewer (Gemini). Subscription-backed via Antigravity CLI (agy-review.ps1) on the user's paid Google plan. Diff-only (repo-blind): pass the key repo files via -ContextPath. The wrapper pins gemini-3.1-pro-high and runs in read-only plan mode.
reviewers.label: Gemini

alternates._comment: Opus is reserved as judge (Phase 3) and verifier (Phase 4) -- not a blind reviewer. Do NOT enable as a reviewer: reviewer==judge collapses the anthropic axis to the adjudicator's model seen twice.
alternates.label: Claude Opus

roles._comment: Judgment roles the host runs after the driver's blind+cross-examine spine. Phase 3 (adjudicate) is a single Opus judge for one coherent voice. Phase 3.5 (judge-audit, opt-in) is a cross-vendor sanity check on the adjudicated report -- default a non-Anthropic vendor. Phase 4 (verify) draws from a CROSS-VENDOR pool (Sonnet/Kimi/Codex), rotated by vendor, so verification is not an Anthropic monoculture. REPO ACCESS IS PER POOL MEMBER, NOT PER ROLE: a role-wide flag silently promoted Kimi -- deliberately repoAccess:false as a reviewer because it has no per-invocation read-only mode -- to a repo-aware verifier that could WRITE to the very tree it was verifying, in the one phase whose entire purpose is trustworthy evidence about that tree. A member with repoAccess:false is given the diff and context files only, or a detached-commit `git worktree`; it is never handed -RepoPath on the live tree.

_sandboxComment: Wrappers with NO hard per-invocation read-only mode. A wrapper listed here must never carry repoAccess:true anywhere in this manifest -- as a reviewer, in a role, or in a role's pool. claude-review.ps1 uses --permission-mode plan and codex-review.ps1 uses --sandbox read-only; kimi-review.ps1 has neither and runs under the CLI's global yolo default, so its only guard is a prompt plus the git working tree. verify-audit-contract.ps1 enforces this.
